Shooter — The Sniper Who Was Betrayed

Shooter (2007) follows Bob Lee Swagger, a former Marine sniper who has withdrawn from society after a mission leaves him deeply disillusioned. Known for his extraordinary skills, Swagger is pulled back into action when government officials ask him to help prevent a planned assassination.

Believing he is working to protect the country, Swagger accepts the assignment. But the mission is actually a carefully planned setup, and he is framed for an assassination he did not commit.

Now hunted by the people who recruited him, Swagger goes on the run and begins uncovering the truth behind the conspiracy. Using his military experience and knowledge of tactical operations, he works to expose the people responsible while trying to survive their attempts to silence him.

As he gets closer to the truth, Swagger realizes the conspiracy reaches much higher than he expected. What started as a mission to protect someone becomes a personal fight to clear his name and reveal the people behind the betrayal.

The film explores themes of betrayal, loyalty, corruption, survival, justice, and revenge. Swagger's greatest advantage is that the people hunting him underestimate just how difficult he is to eliminate.

What makes Shooter compelling is its combination of precision, action, conspiracy, and a protagonist who refuses to stay down after being betrayed.

💬 They framed the wrong man—and now he's coming back for everyone who betrayed him.

source_details.synopsis: Shooter is a 2007 American action thriller film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by Jonathan Lemkin, based on the 1993 novel Point of Impact by Stephen Hunter. The film follows Force Recon Marine Scout Sniper veteran Bob Lee Swagger (Mark Wahlberg), who is framed for murder by a mercenary unit operating for a private military firm. The film also stars Michael Peña, Danny Glover, Kate Mara, Levon Helm, and Ned Beatty. Shooter was produced by Lorenzo di Bonaventura through di Bonaventura Pictures, and released by Paramount Pictures in the United States on March 23, 2007. The film received mixed reviews and grossed $95.7 million on a $61 million budget.
